disposition.description: Exactly one truthful state per artifact. 'implemented_and_consumed' is the only state that claims a real consumer decides the rows; tools/test_run_sarf_evals.py proves that claim by mutating the consumer and requiring the bank to go red.

repo_path.description: Repo-relative path with forward slashes. Absolute and server paths are forbidden.

description: The contract tools/run_sarf_evals.py executes. It fixes, for every Sarf eval artifact and every Store A rule file (sarf/rules/*.json), exactly one disposition, the adapter that runs it, the real consumer modules invoked, what is and is NOT enforced, the pinned measurements of live consumer behaviour, and the follow-on packet for every remaining gap. This file certifies nothing and promotes nothing: the sarf@2.1-@2.4 increments stay CANDIDATE and the runner asserts sarf/SKILL.md still says so. Executable twin: run_sarf_evals.validate_contract().

banks.description: One row per artifact under sarf/evals/. Every artifact must appear exactly once.

adapter.description: The run_sarf_evals adapter that executes this bank. Adapters invoke production consumers; an adapter that only restates the bank's own fields is not permitted to carry the implemented_and_consumed disposition.

behavioral_consumer.description: The production DECISION function this bank's adapter invokes per row (module:function), or null. Required, and restricted to the decision consumers, when the disposition is implemented_and_consumed. Normalization helpers never qualify.

consumers.description: The production modules this bank's adapter actually invokes. Required to be non-empty when the disposition is implemented_and_consumed.

enforced_properties.description: The exact behavioural properties this bank's adapter proves. Plain statements, one per property.

followup_packet.description: Packet id under qamus/task-packets/ that specifies the missing consumer, or null when nothing is outstanding. Required for candidate_no_consumer and fixture_only.

form.description: jsonl = one row per line; object = a JSON object whose row_key names the cases[]/assertions[] array. Both forms are row-counted.

loc_fields.description: Fields that must hold a surah:ayah:word address when present.

metric_floors.description: Diagnostics that record a KNOWN-WRONG state and must be allowed to improve. Compared with >=, never with equality, so a later repair cannot fail the gate. A metric may be pinned or floored, never both.

not_enforced_properties.description: What this runner deliberately does NOT decide. Keeping the unsupported categories visible is a requirement, not an omission.

pinned_metrics.description: Measured behaviour of the LIVE consumer, pinned so drift in either direction is a red gate. A pin is a measurement, never a copy of the bank's own expectations.

property_coverage.description: Coverage at PROPERTY granularity. A row may be decided for one property and uncovered for another, so a successful assertion may never hide an unproven one. `decided_by` is either a production decision callable or `structural:<module>` (a normalizer/shape assertion, which is never behavioural coverage); `applicable_rows` is verified against the adapter's observed per-property evaluation count; `covered` may be true only for a decision callable.

row_key.description: For object-form artifacts, the array key that holds the rows (cases / assertions). Null for jsonl.

secondary_consumers.description: Consumers a bank invokes only for a SUBSET of its rows. Each row declares the callable, the applicability in plain words and the exact expected call count, which the runner verifies against proxies it installs. A conditional consumer may never be sold as the per-row one.

candidate_boundary_surfaces.description: The repository surfaces the candidate-boundary check cross-joins candidate rule ids against: the projector registry, the certification stores and any record file that could carry a public-materialization flag or target. Declaring them explicitly means a new surface must be reviewed rather than silently unscanned.

candidate_increments_not_promoted.description: The standing non-promotion record for the four CANDIDATE increments in sarf/SKILL.md.

expected_projector_registrations_citing_.description: How many registrations cite a candidate rule id. An unexpected registration must be reviewed, not silently absorbed.

projector_registry.description: The registered-projector file joined to the candidate rule ids.

registry_files.description: increment id -> the rule-registry JSONL whose rows must all stay status=candidate.

disposition_definitions.description: The four dispositions defined in this repository's own words. All four must be defined even when a state is unused by the current banks.

store_a_rules.description: One row per sarf/rules/*.json file. A row may only claim implemented_and_consumed if a named module actually reads the file; the runner proves this against the repository, not against prose.

consumption_kind.description: How production code uses the file. data_driven = rule CONTENT changes or is rejected by a production decision, proven by a bounded mutation prover; id_citation = only stable ids are read to build a citation while the operative condition is hard-coded; existence_gate = the harness only asserts the file exists/parses; none = nothing executable reads it. Only data_driven may carry implemented_and_consumed.

title: Sarf eval runner contract v1
